message.content:
**Answer:** The sculpture most often cited as the *iconic* masterpiece of the 19th‑century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin** (1889). --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Date** | 1889 (late 19th century) | | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, French sculptor | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist, dramatic use of form and texture | | **Impact** | • Became Rodin’s first major public success.
• Influenced modern sculpture with its expressive, almost unfinished surface.
• Widely reproduced, displayed in museums worldwide, and referenced in countless works of art and popular culture. | | **Legacy** | • Often considered Rodin’s “signature” piece.
• Frequently compared to his later “The Thinker” (1902) as the most recognizable of his oeuvre. | --- ### Other contenders from the 19th century | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it matters | |-----------|--------|------|----------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Rodin | 1880–1917 (unfinished) | Massive, complex work that pushed the limits of bronze casting and narrative sculpture. | | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Bartholdi | 1886 | Monumental public sculpture symbolizing freedom; a global icon. | | **The Venus de Milo** (re‑exhibited) | Unknown (Greek) | Re‑discovered 1820 | Though ancient, its 19th‑century rediscovery sparked renewed interest in classical sculpture. | | **The Thinker** | Rodin | 1902–1904 | Technically 20th century, but often grouped with late‑19th century modernism. | --- ### Bottom line While the 19th century produced many groundbreaking works, **Rodin’s “The Kiss”** is the sculpture most frequently identified as the era’s most famous and enduringly popular piece. It captures the artistic shift toward expressive realism and remains a touchstone for both art historians and the general public.
